text: MEA campaign at ENTP lasted for approximately 1 month. ION operated for 12 hours per day from September 28, 2023, to October 17, 2023. ION operated for a total of 250 hours with MEA, capturing 76 tonnes of CO . 2 The goal of the MEA campaign was to determine the baseline performance of a common carbon capture solvent on the custom built ENTP system. Unfortunately, there was significant foaming in the stripper during MEA operations, a phenomenon that has been observed during startup of other MEA campaigns1. ION added anti-foam to the system, but while it initially stopped the foaming, the effectiveness diminished over time. As a result, it was difficult to determine accurate SRDs for MEA because the foam prevented a significant amount of heat transfer in the stripper. Thus, ION did not observe the typical relationship between capture efficiency and SRD where the duty increases with increasing capture efficiency. There was also no way to account for foaming in the postprocessing of the data. Capture efficiency with MEA ranged from approximately 60 to 90%. SRDs ranged from 4.5 to 6.7 GJ/tCO . The liquid flow to gas flow ratio (L/G) was typically above 1. The high L/G ratio during MEA 2 operations may have also contributed to the poor performance observed with MEA as the ENTP system is designed specifically to ION solvent specifications, which operate at significantly lower L/G ratios due to their higher solvent capacity compared to MEA. ION sampled the MEA solvent daily to measure solvent degradation rates and decomposition product buildup. Solvent samples were sent to ION’s Boulder laboratory to undergo various analyses. The graph of the MEA lean side composition closure is shown below in Figure 9-1. The lean side composition closure refers to the closure in the mass balance of the various components in the lean solvent. ION measures the concentration of various compounds in the solvent, including water, CO , and solvent components. The independently determined concentrations are 2 then summed. Ideally, the sum is 100%, which means that all mass in the solvent is accounted for. When the solvent begins to degrade, the sum is less than 100%, and the missing mass can be attributed to liquid degradation products. A picture of the MEA samples over the first week of operations is also included in Figure 9-2. Degradation products are often longer-chain molecules that cause color changes in the solvent.
